newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Danzas sets capital structuring, payout.
newsitem.headline: Danzas sets capital structuring, payout.

text.p: Freight forwarder Danzas AG said its board of directors had agreed to simplify the capital structure and use resulting cash for an extraordinary payment to shareholders of 26.2 million Swiss francs.
"The ordinary dividend payment for the 1996 financial year will not be affected by this one-time extraordinary partial repayment of capital," a Danzas statement said.
It also said the board had approved a stock option plan for Danzas management.
The capital reorganisation must be approved by the annual shareholder meeting on June 6, it said.
Danzas said it would replace existing registered shares and participation certificates with a registered share having a lower nominal value.
The resulting total share capital of 52.4 million Swiss francs would be halved to 26.2 million Swiss francs by paying out the difference to shareholders, it said.
"The repayment amount of 10 Swiss francs per share is to be paid to the shareholders in cash," Danzas said.
It said the ordinary dividend would be set separately based on 1996 figures and would be "at least at the level of the previous year."
Danzas said the capital simplification and pay back was part of a transition to shareholder-friendly policies under a new management philosophy launched in late 1995.
It said 400,000 existing registered shares with a face value of 100 Swiss francs each would be split into two million 20-franc shares.
The existing 620,000 participartion certificates worth a nominal 20 francs each would be converted into registered shares with the same nominal value.
In addition, the Danzas board said it had decided to offer stock options to about 150 uper-level managers as a means of encouraging the group's performance.
The options would be offered from spring of this year from a pool of 100,000 registered shares set aside after the restructuring for the next few years.
The options could be exercised three years after issue at the earliest and would expire five years after issue, Danzas said.
